text: In the village called Ramgar, a boy named Raghav lived with [music] his mother and father. Raghav's father Sudhir worked as a laborer in the village and whatever he earned was used to run the family. Raghav studied in 11th [music] standard. One after school, he saw a boy drinking mango drink in a bottle. When he saw that, Raghav also felt like drinking it. In the evening, Raghav said to his father, "Father, I need some money." Money? Why do you have some work? Father, I want to drink that mango drink. Many [clears throat] children in my school drink it everyday. So, I also want to drink it. [music] It looks so nice. So, the taste must be just as good. Son, I do not have so much money right now. I will get it for you some other time. Now you focus on your studies. If you study well, then you will never [music] lack anything in life. But father, I also want to live like other children to eat and drink like them. You always say this and then I never get it. Please give me the money. >> Raghav, is this how you talk to your father? Let your father wash his hands and face. And listen, if you want mango drink, I'll make it for you at home. >> No mom, I do not want to drink mango drink made at home. I want the one from the shop only. >> Son, you know our situation. We somehow manage our daily needs with great difficulty. >> Yes, yes, I know everything, Mom. But I want money right now. That's it. So, give me money. Seeing this Ragha walked out angrily. His parents were laborers but they had raised Ragha with a lot of love. He was very smart but sometimes when he thought about their condition he become [music] angry. Sudhir called out Raghav Raghav come here son do not be angry son. Even after his father called him, Ragha went [music] outside. Then Sudhir said, "Shallini, Ragha is not wrong. We cannot even fulfill one small wish of our only son. Tomorrow while coming back, I will see if I can get some advance from the owner." >> There is no need for that. I'll make it for him at home. Anyway, it is summer now. So, we get mangoes in the market and mango drink is just sweet mango pulp [music] only. >> The next day while coming back, Charini brought some mangoes and made a mango pulp juice. >> Ragha, see what I have made for you? Mango drink. This is what you wanted to have, right? >> I do not want to drink this mango drink

from home. You drink it. I want the one bought from the shop only. Raghav, your mother has made this with so much effort for you. At least taste a little. If you do not like it, then I myself will bring the bottled mango [music] drink for you today. Okay. Are you telling the truth, father? Yes, son. Absolutely. Hearing his father's words, Raghov tasted the mango drink. He liked it a lot. He finished the entire glass and said to his mother, "Mom, this is very good. I liked it a lot. Father, now I do not want the mango drink from the market. From now on, I will only drink mango drink made by mom. Mom, will you give me some for school tomorrow?" Now, Raghav hugged his parents. That night, after dinner, everyone went to sleep. The next day, Raghav took the mango drink to school and shared it with his friends. Some children started teasing him, but a few of his friends tasted the drink and liked it very much. Raghav's friend Surat said, "Raghav, this is so good. Your mother has made it better than the drink we get outside." Yes, you are right. Hey, hey, whatever. It is just a mango drink from home. What is so special about it? Taste it once then you will know. That second boy also [music] tasted it and liked it a lot. Now the children started asking Raghav everyday to bring mango drink. Some days passed like this. One day Sudhir fell very ill. He become worried about the future. Sudhir looked tense for many days. Seeing this, Raghav asked, "Father, what happened? Why are you so tense these days? Tell me what happened." [cough] Uh, nothing, son. Nothing much. Father, tell me what is the matter. >> [cough] >> Son, all these days I worked hard and earned money. So somehow our house ran properly. But now my health is getting worse. So all the work has to be done by your mother alone. That's why I'm worried. [cough] Father, your health is already not good. Please do not think about all this. You just rest. Okay. Now Raghav thought even when father is sick he's thinking

about the house. Now I [music] have to do something and take responsibility. After school I must work. Then Raghav told his mother to buy good mangoes from the field. He took them, kept them in a basket and went out into the village to sell them. Hey mango boy, how much for the mangoes? 50 rupees per kg, sir. 50 rupees per kg. It's expensive, sir. It's not expensive. Go and see the rate in the market. Mangoes are very costly there. These have ripened well on the tree. If you eat them once, you will buy only from me again. All right, then give me 2 kgs. But give me best ones. On the first day, Raghav sold 5 kgs of mangoes quickly. Now he started selling mangoes everyday and gave his earnings to his parents. One day when Raghav went to sell mangoes in the village, his friend [music] Sudhir met him. Hey Raghav, what are you doing? Sudhir, father is not well now. I thought exams are already over and the holidays will start soon. So I should help him a little. All right, but why don't you do one thing? Make good mango drink and sell it. You will earn more profit. And anyways, auntie makes such tasty mango drink. Its taste is still in my mouth. M I still remember it. Oh yes, Sudir, I did not even think about that. Ra went home and told everything to his mother. The next day along with mangoes, he took the mango drink made with his mother's help and went to the village to sell it. Some people made fun of [music] him. But a few people tasted his mango drink and they also liked it very [music] much. Raghav sold a glass of mango drink for five rupees. [music] One villager said, "Hey brothers, he's selling mango drink like this. Who drinks mango drink [music] like this? Real mango drink comes in bottles. That is the tasty one." Raghav did not pay attention to his words. Raghav's friends came with their parents to drink his mango drink. They also liked it more than the bottle drink. Now [music] Raghav started making a lot of mango drink everyday with his mother and [music] when he went to the village it would finish quickly. Slowly his mother's homemade mango drink become famous not only in their village but also in the nearby villages. Now Raghav's mother left her labor work and started [music] going with Raghav. When Raghav had saved some money, he rented a

small shop. One day the same man who had laughed at him earlier came and said, "Son, I had made fun of your mango drink before. But today, after my son told me, I tasted it. Truly, everything else is nothing compared to your mango drink. It is very tasty. God bless you, my son." Thank you, sir. This is my mother's homemade mango drink. It had to be tasty. While Raghav and the men were talking, another villager came to him and said, "Hey Raghav, uh my daughter's wedding is after 10 days. Uh I need uh 500 glasses of mango drink." "Sure, sir, you will get it. Do not worry, but you will have to give some advance money. Hope it is okay for you." Oh, of course, son. I here take these 5,000 rupees as advance. Raghav took the money and completed this big first order of his life on time. Slowly Raghav started getting orders for feddings and parties. For parties, he packed the mango drink in bottles and supplied it. Step [music] by step, he began packing his mango drink and selling it in the nearby city as well. Seeing his success at such a young age, his parents felt very happy. Now Raghav got his father treated [music] properly and the whole family started living happily together.
